description: Ubuntu LTS, Node LTS, Prisma, PostgreSQL and digest-pinned OCI baseline.
compatibility_rules: Node must be an upstream LTS version supported by the selected Prisma major.
Prisma 7.9.1 requires Node ^20.19, ^22.12 or >=24.0, TypeScript >=5.4 and same-version prisma, @prisma/client and @prisma/adapter-pg packages.
next@16.3.0 accepts React/react-dom ^19.0.0; the catalog requires both npm packages to use the same audited stable exact version, while project build/browser compatibility remains required.
A transition selects exactly one component per slot, requires an absolute HTTPS migration Issue plus one matching unexpired exception, and never permits a prohibited component.
Next.js 14 is recorded as prohibited evidence and intentionally has no transition allowlist entry.
PostgreSQL major adoption requires a separate backup, restore and rollback-capable project Change.
Every production OCI base and application image is identified by sha256 digest; mutable-only tags fail closed.

constraints.deployment: docker-release/v1 is preferred; pm2-legacy only describes delivery ownership and does not grant deployment capability.
constraints.data_storage: PostgreSQL data resides on approved local or managed persistent storage, never an application container layer.
constraints.concurrency: Database connection and worker limits are owned and load-tested by each application Change.
constraints.availability: Availability topology is declared outside this architecture lock and remains owned by host/release governance.
constraints.backup: A database major Change requires a verified backup before mutation.
constraints.restore_drill: A restore drill is required before production adoption of a new PostgreSQL major.
